terms.heading: Terms
terms.unavailable: The contract terms are unavailable right now.

staking.title: Staking
staking.yieldRateNote: Simple, not compounding — yield never folds back into the earning base, so what you earn is a function of stake and time and nothing else.
staking.withdrawalsNote: Staking is not locked. A withdrawal is limited only by what your debt allows: enough collateral has to stay to keep the position above the liquidation threshold.

borrowing.title: Borrowing
borrowing.maxLtvNote: The most you may borrow against your stake. A borrow that would cross this is refused rather than allowed and then liquidated.
borrowing.thresholdNote: Where the health factor reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible.
borrowing.thresholdNoteGap: Where the health factor reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible. The gap above the LTV ceiling is deliberate: it is the room a position has to accrue interest before anyone can touch it.
borrowing.kinkNote: Where the borrow rate stops rising gently and starts rising steeply, so lenders are paid to refill a pool that is running dry.

liquidated.title: If you are liquidated
liquidated.closeFactorNote: The most of your debt one liquidation may clear. It caps what a single price dip costs you — the rest of the position survives it.
liquidated.bonusNote: The discount a liquidator takes on the collateral they seize, paid out of your position. It is what makes anyone show up to close an underwater loan, which is what keeps the pool solvent.
liquidated.fullNote: Below this health factor the close-factor cap is lifted and the whole lien may be cleared at once. It is derived on chain from the threshold and the bonus, not configured — it is precisely the point where a capped liquidation stops making a position healthier.

rounds.title: Taking a position
rounds.intro: Odds come from how the pool splits, so the protocol never takes the other side of your view.
rounds.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement, so it is already inside the odds you were shown rather than deducted from a win afterwards.
rounds.entryCutoffNote: Entry closes before the round locks so nobody can take a side in the last second against a price they can already see moving.
rounds.minimumPerSideNote: A round whose losing side never reaches this is voided and every stake is refunded in full — a one-sided pool has nothing to pay a winner from.

fees.heading: Protocol earnings
fees.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement. A voided round takes none at all — rake is only recorded on the resolve path — so a market on a slow feed earns nothing while it is voiding.
fees.rakeBound: Capped by the rake collected, not by the token balance, so this cannot reach stakes still owed to users — including a resolved round's unclaimed winnings.
fees.reservesNote: The protocol's cut of borrower interest, credited when interest accrues into the index rather than when a borrower pays.
fees.reservesBound: Subordinated to suppliers: a withdrawal is refused unless the pool still holds enough cash to meet every supplier claim afterwards. Credited interest that nobody has paid is not withdrawable.
fees.predatesTreasury: This contract was deployed before the stored treasury and has no treasury(). Its withdrawal still takes a destination, so it can only be called from a terminal — that is the state GHO-40 is about, and it clears on the next deploy.
fees.overAccrued: More than has accrued. The contract would refuse this.

stake.title: Stake
stake.subtitle: Earns while it sits, and backs everything you borrow
stake.needsWallet: Your stake, what it earns, and what you can borrow against it all live at your address.
stake.notConfigured: No stake vault is configured for this network.
stake.approveAnd: {mode, select, deposit {Approve and deposit} other {Approve and withdraw}}
stake.overMax: {mode, select, deposit {That is more than your wallet holds.} other {That is more than you have deposited.}}
stake.partialExitBlocked: You have debt open against this position, so it can only be withdrawn in full. The lien is settled from the proceeds and the rest comes back to you.
stake.neverLeaves: Your stake never leaves to back a loan — borrowing places a lien against it and the funds come from the lending pool. It keeps earning the whole time, which is the point: you take a view without unwinding your savings.

borrow.title: Borrow
borrow.subtitle: Draw against your collateral, or repay what you owe
borrow.needsWallet: Borrowing capacity is a property of your deposited collateral.
borrow.notConfigured: No vault is configured for this network.
borrow.overDebt: More than you owe. Repaying is capped at the debt.
borrow.interestNote: Interest accrues every second at the pool’s current rate, so the debt grows on its own between transactions. Borrowing stops at the LTV ceiling, which sits well below the liquidation line.

lend.title: Lend
lend.subtitle: Supply the pool that borrowers draw from, and earn what they pay
lend.notConfigured: No lending pool is configured for this network.
lend.unreadableDetail: The RPC call failed. Any balance you have supplied is unchanged — this screen just cannot see it right now.

warnings.exit-blocked: Every token in the pool is out on loan, so nothing can be withdrawn right now. Your balance keeps earning, and liquidity returns as borrowers repay.
warnings.exit-limited: More of your balance is out on loan than the pool holds in cash, so only part of it can be withdrawn right now. The rest returns as borrowers repay.
warnings.past-kink: The pool is lent out past its target, which is why the rate is high. The same fact makes exiting harder: the rate is steep here to pull supply in and slow borrowing down.

lend.connectToSupplyDetail: The pool figures above are the same for everyone. A supply balance is per address.

pool.heading: The lending pool
pool.borrowersPay: borrowers pay , and that is where the supply rate comes from
pool.utilizationNote: Utilization is the fraction of the pool that is out on loan. It is what you earn — idle liquidity pays nobody — and it is what stands between you and the exit, because money that is lent out is not money you can withdraw. The two readings are the whole decision.

lend.overLiquidity: More than the pool holds in cash. {amount} {symbol} is available right now — the rest of your balance is out as someone else’s loan and comes back as borrowers repay.
lend.supplyNote: Supplying lowers utilization, and with it the rate you are about to earn — the curve prices scarcity, so adding liquidity makes it less scarce. The figure above is the rate's input after your deposit lands.
lend.withdrawNote: Withdrawing raises utilization for everyone left in the pool, which raises the borrow rate and the supply rate together. Past the target the curve turns steep on purpose.

liquidate.title: Liquidate
liquidate.subtitle: Positions past the line, and what closing them pays
liquidate.notConfigured: No vault is configured for this network.
liquidate.unreadable: Could not read the borrower list
liquidate.empty: Nobody is carrying debt right now.
liquidate.emptyDetail: Every borrower the indexer has seen is listed here, healthy or not — an empty list means there are none, not that none are at risk.
liquidate.scanned: {count, plural, one {# borrower scanned} other {# borrowers scanned}}
liquidate.sources: Names come from the indexer, which has every borrow and repayment. Figures are read from the chain at the head, so a health factor here is current.
liquidate.truncated: The scan cap was reached, so there may be more borrowers than these. The ones shown are those with the largest debt — a truncated list is missing the trivia, not the risk.
liquidate.underwaterLoses: Underwater, but a liquidation loses money here
liquidate.connectToWriteOff: Connect a wallet to write off
liquidate.writeOffNote: Owes more than it holds, so no liquidation closes it. Pays you nothing; it ends the position and charges the loss to reserves, then to suppliers.
liquidate.youNeed: {scope} · you need {amount} {symbol} approved to the vault
